name: HUMPIRE OVERCLOCK
tagline: Enhancer for density, harmonics and loudness, with a Power knob and a two-band split.
gumroad_title: HUMPIRE OVERCLOCK - Enhancer VST3 + AU Plugin (12 Presets) | Density, Harmonics, Loudness
summary: An enhancer plugin that adds density, harmonics and perceived loudness with a Power knob, curve control and a two-band split.
about: HUMPIRE OVERCLOCK splits the signal into a low band and a high band at an adjustable frequency (80 Hz to 4 kHz) and saturates each band with 2x oversampling. The low band gets density, the high band gets generated harmonics.

POWER sets the overall drive, CURVE morphs from a soft asymmetric curve to a hard clip, DENSITY mixes the low-band saturation in and HARMONICS sets the high-band harmonics. The output is level-compensated so more power does not mean a much louder signal.
On the screen, a ring and an animated fan follow the Power setting.

features.d: One control for the overall drive, with level compensation.
From a soft, asymmetric curve to a hard clip.
Low-band density and high-band harmonics are set separately.
Split frequency from 80 Hz to 4 kHz.
Saturation runs oversampled to limit aliasing.
Factory presets grouped by category, user presets saved by name, A/B compare, undo and redo.
Scales from 50% to 200% with the proportions locked. Simple and Clean display modes.

includes: HUMPIRE OVERCLOCK plugin (Windows VST3; macOS VST3 + Audio Unit)

faq.q: Which DAWs does it work in?
faq.a: It is a VST3 effect on Windows and macOS, plus Audio Unit on macOS. It is designed for FL Studio and should load in any host that supports these formats.
Yes, the small latency of its 2x oversampling filters, which the plugin reports to your host.

faq.q: Can I save my own presets?
faq.a: Yes. The SAVE button stores the current settings under a name you choose, and they appear in the User category of the preset menu.
